# fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests (Data Source)

Every Proxmox guest in the organization, across every cluster -- the fleet-wide counterpart of `fivenines_proxmox_cluster_guests`.

Group by `proxmox_cluster_id` to split the list back into clusters, or narrow to one with the filter of the same name. No deduplication is needed: guests are cluster-scoped and only the authoritative reporter writes them, so each appears exactly once however many hosts report its cluster.

A GUEST MIGRATES: `vmid` is unique cluster-wide and the row is keyed on cluster + vmid, so `node_name` is where the guest lives right now, not a stable attribute of it.

`stale` here is the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold, matching what every guest trigger reads.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every Proxmox guest in the organization, across every cluster -- the
# fleet-wide counterpart of fivenines_proxmox_cluster_guests. No deduplication
# is needed: guests are cluster-scoped and only the authoritative reporter
# writes them, so each appears exactly once however many hosts report a cluster.
data "fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests" "all" {}

# Every stopped VM in the fleet, filtered server-side
data "fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests" "stopped_vms" {
  status     = "stopped"
  guest_type = "vm"
}

# Group the fleet back into clusters. proxmox_cluster_id is the uuid
# fivenines_proxmox_clusters publishes as `id` -- NOT the cluster_key a metric
# query takes.
output "guests_per_cluster" {
  value = {
    for id in distinct(data.fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests.all.organization_proxmox_guests[*].proxmox_cluster_id) :
    id => length([
      for g in data.fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests.all.organization_proxmox_guests :
      g.vmid if g.proxmox_cluster_id == id
    ])
  }
}

# Or narrow to one cluster server-side instead of filtering in HCL.
#
# An unknown cluster uuid is a 400 naming it, never an empty list -- the
# organization's clusters are a closed vocabulary, and an empty list would be an
# all-clear for a cluster nobody can see. So interpolate a real id rather than
# pasting a literal.
data "fivenines_organization_proxmox_guests" "one_cluster" {
  proxmox_cluster_id = one([
    for c in data.fivenines_proxmox_clusters.all.proxmox_clusters :
    c.id if c.name == "pve-prod"
  ])
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `guest_type` (String) Filter by guest kind. One of: `vm`, `lxc`.
- `proxmox_cluster_id` (String) Narrow to one cluster. The uuid the guest rows publish as `proxmox_cluster_id` and `fivenines_proxmox_clusters` publishes as `id` -- NOT the `cluster_key` that `fivenines_metric_query` takes.

AN UNKNOWN CLUSTER ID IS AN ERROR, NEVER AN EMPTY LIST. The organization's clusters are a closed vocabulary, so a uuid belonging to another organization -- or to a cluster that no longer exists -- is rejected with a 400 naming it as unknown, and a malformed value is a 400 asking for a UUID. That is deliberate: an empty list would be an all-clear for a cluster nobody can see, and would disagree with `fivenines_proxmox_cluster_guests`, which 404s for the same id.
- `q` (String) Case-insensitive substring match on the guest name or vmid.
- `stale` (Boolean) Freshness filter, built on the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold here -- matching what every guest trigger reads, and NOT the fixed ten minutes the nodes and storages data sources use. Omit for both.
- `status` (String) Filter by guest state. One of: `unknown`, `stopped`, `running`, `paused`, `suspended`.
- `updated_since` (String) Return only rows whose `updated_at` is at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp. Inclusive, so a row updated in the same instant as the cursor comes back rather than falling through the gap. The ingester touches `updated_at` on every agent tick, so this is a freshness filter rather than a change feed, and there are no tombstones: a row the agent stops reporting is deleted.

### Read-Only

- `organization_proxmox_guests` (Attributes List) The rows the cluster's authoritative reporter wrote. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--organization_proxmox_guests))

<a id="nestedatt--organization_proxmox_guests"></a>
### Nested Schema for `organization_proxmox_guests`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String) When this row was first recorded. This is when the agent first happened to report it, not anything an operator would recognize.
- `guest_type` (String) A full VM or an LXC container -- genuinely different things behind one Proxmox API. One of: `vm`, `lxc`.
- `id` (String) Row identifier.
- `last_synced_at` (String) Server arrival time of the tick that last refreshed this row (never the agent's clock). Null when the row has never synced.
- `name` (String) The guest name as Proxmox reports it. Null when unnamed; `vmid` is the identity.
- `node_name` (String) The hosting node's name, denormalized so a row is legible without a second call. Null only if the node row went missing.
- `proxmox_cluster_id` (String) The cluster this guest belongs to -- the uuid `fivenines_proxmox_clusters` publishes as `id`, and the key to group this fleet-wide list by. NOT the `cluster_key` that `fivenines_metric_query` takes.
- `proxmox_node_id` (String) The node currently hosting the guest. Changes on migration.
- `stale` (Boolean) Measured against the ORGANIZATION's offline threshold, matching what every guest trigger, the fleet grid and the workflow engine read. This is a DIFFERENT window from the one ProxmoxNode and ProxmoxStorage use (a fixed ten minutes), so the same age can read stale here and fresh there. The divergence is the product's, and the endpoints reproduce it rather than agreeing with each other at the cost of agreeing with the alerts.
- `state_changed_at` (String) When `status` last changed -- the field that turns "it is stopped" into "it has been stopped since 04:10", and the one the guest-status trigger reads.
- `status` (String) `unknown` is a real value: it is what an unrecognized Proxmox state maps to, and means "we could not classify it", not "the guest is gone". One of: `unknown`, `stopped`, `running`, `paused`, `suspended`.
- `updated_at` (String) When this row was last written. The ingester touches it on every agent tick, so it is a freshness stamp rather than a change feed.
- `vmid` (String) The Proxmox id an operator recognizes ("VM 1042"). A STRING, because that is how Proxmox reports it and how the row is keyed.
